passage: Picture my birthday guest list: forty names and one gap. That gap was Ritu, after the joke about my haircut in front of the whole class. For a week I ran the plan in my head, and it felt fantastic. I could see the invitation going round and Ritu standing there, not on it. Then I remembered what Ritu told me last year: "When people get annoyed with me, they just stop including me." Ritu was afraid of exactly this. If I did it, I would not be teaching anything; I would be handing over proof. And I would lose the one person who still laughs at my worst jokes. The daydream stayed sweet only as long as I did not think about Ritu's face. I'm Deepak, and I nearly typed that list.

qa.q: How many names were on Deepak's birthday guest list?
qa.a: The guest list had forty names and one gap.

qa.q: What was Deepak feeling while running the plan in mind for a week, and what changed?
qa.a: Deepak felt satisfied and vengeful at first, but the feeling soured when Deepak remembered Ritu's fear of being left out.

qa.q: What alternative could Deepak try instead of leaving Ritu out, and why?
qa.a: Deepak could tell Ritu privately that the haircut joke hurt and invite Ritu anyway, because it addresses the hurt without confirming Ritu's fear.

qa.q: How would Ritu see being left off the list?
qa.a: Ritu would likely feel that the fear of being dropped when someone is annoyed had come true, and might pull away from Deepak.

grounding: The student plans to leave the friend out of a birthday party to hurt back, which feels satisfying in imagination but would prove the friend's fear right and cost a friendship worth keeping.

passage: I'm Zainab's older cousin, and I was helping with her birthday invitations when she crossed out Kavitha's name. Hard. "She told everyone I copied her project," Zainab said. "Let's see how she likes being left out." She was smiling as she said it, a tight little smile I didn't like. I knew Kavitha had once told Zainab her biggest fear was being the one nobody picks. I think Zainab knew that too. The invitations went out on Tuesday. On Saturday, at the party, Zainab kept checking her phone. Kavitha had changed her status to a single line: "I knew it." Zainab put the phone face down and didn't eat her cake. I don't know if she felt guilty, but she didn't look like someone who had won.

qa.q: Whose name did Zainab cross out?
What does Zainab's tight little smile suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she felt a bitter kind of satisfaction imagining Kavitha hurt, though mixed with something uneasy.

qa.q: What else could Zainab have done about the project rumour?
qa.a: Asked Kavitha directly why she said it and told her how it hurt, instead of hitting back through the party.

qa.q: What does Kavitha's status show about how she sees being left out?
qa.a: It shows Kavitha feels her fear of being the one nobody picks has come true, which makes repair much harder.

grounding: An observer watches a student leave a friend out of her party to hurt back, confirming the friend's fear and costing the friendship.

passage:
Monday. Hansa laughs when the class reads Suraj's awful exam answer aloud. Suraj goes home and, lying on his bed, plans his revenge: his birthday party on Saturday, everyone invited except Hansa. He imagines her face when she hears. It feels great.
Wednesday. He tells three friends the plan, grinning. "She's always scared people will drop her. Well." One of them looks uncomfortable.
Saturday. The party is loud and fun, but Suraj keeps glancing at the door.
Sunday. Hansa's message arrives: "I heard why I wasn't invited. I always thought one day you'd get bored of me. I guess I was right." Suraj reads it four times. The revenge had felt sweet on Monday. Now he just feels like he threw away the person who has sat next to him since Class 3.

qa.q: How did Suraj feel imagining Hansa's face on Monday?
qa.a: He felt a hot, satisfying pleasure at the thought of hurting her back after being laughed at.

qa.q: What could Suraj have done on Monday instead?
qa.a: Told Hansa it hurt when she laughed at his answer, giving her a chance to apologise before revenge made it worse.

qa.q: How does Hansa see being left out?
qa.a: Hansa takes it as proof of her old fear that Suraj would get bored of her one day.

grounding: Shows over a week how revenge by leaving a friend out of a party feels sweet in imagination but confirms her fear and costs the friendship.
